reports.findingsIntro: We reviewed the City of Anaheim's Accessory Dwelling Unit Submittal Requirements Checklist (Z412) (dated NOV 2025) against State ADU Law (Gov. Code, §§ 66310–66342) on 2026-11-07. Of its 8 lines, 1 may not match current state law, as noted below.

findings.quote:
☐ 1. OWNER OCCUPANCY COVENANT: AMC Section 18.38.015.110 requires the recordation of an owner occupancy covenant for all JADUs, authorized by the California Government Code Sections 65852.2 and 65852.22. The covenant for the JADU will be drafted by the City Attorney’s office and must be recorded with the Orange County Clerk-Recorder’s office prior to the issuance of a building permit. The covenant will specify the following, at a minimum:
▪ The JADU shall not be sold or owned separately from the main dwelling and the parcel upon which the unit is located and shall not be subdivided in any manner that would authorize such sale or ownership;
▪ Owner occupancy is required within one of the dwelling units on the property; and
▪ Owner occupancy shall be binding upon any successor in ownership of the property.
findings.stateRule: Gov. Code, § 66333, subd. (b) requires owner occupancy for a JADU only when it shares sanitation facilities with the main house. It isn't required when the JADU has its own bathroom, or when the owner is a governmental agency, land trust or housing organization. Separately, SB 477 (2024) renumbered Gov. Code, §§ 65852.2 and 65852.22 as §§ 66310–66342.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 65852.2 and 65852.22 with Gov. Code, § 66333, and apply the owner-occupancy clause only to JADUs that share sanitation with the main house.

auditTable.line: Planning staff reviews Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs) to determine compliance with applicable zoning code requirements during the Building Division’s plan check review process. This checklist provides an overview of the Planning Services Division’s submittal requirements, in addition to the Building Division’s plan submittal requirements. All accessory dwelling unit requirements can be found in Anaheim Municipal Code (AMC) Section 18.38.015. Visit Anaheim.net/ADUheim for detailed information on developing ADUs in Anaheim and for updates on special programs and incentives that support ADU development. For new detached ADUs, your property may be eligible for the ADU Express Program which provides one day permitting and zero design costs. Visit Anaheim.net/ADUexpress for more information.
auditTable.note: This is an information line. It cites local code only (AMC 18.38.015) and no state statute. The AMC text wasn't checked today, so we can't confirm the section is current.

auditTable.line: ☐ 1. SEWER DEFICIENCY VERIFICATION: Provide a copy of written verification from the Public Works Department verifying that there is sewer capacity to add an ADU to the property. This written verification may be obtained by submitting an email request to the Public Works Department to PWPermits@anaheim.net. Please allow up to four days to receive a reply to your email inquiry.
auditTable.note: No legal authority is cited for the sewer check. State law lets a city limit where ADUs go based on sewer adequacy (Gov. Code, § 66314, subd. (a)), but HCD says those limits can't block § 66323 units (Handbook p. 42). The checklist's 'up to four days' reply isn't tied to the state clock.

auditTable.line: ☐ 2. METER SPOT REPORT: Complete this step if you are adding a new electric meter, upgrading an existing meter, and/or relocating an existing meter. Request a meter sport report inspection online (Anaheim.net/3472) or by calling 714-765-6847. A utility inspector will contact you within two to three business days and provide you a copy of the meter spot report. Include the meter spot report on your building plan check submittal.
auditTable.note: No legal authority is cited for the meter spot report. It's a utility step that applies only when a meter is added, upgraded or moved.

auditTable.line: ☐ 3. NEW ADDRESS REQUEST: Complete this step prior to plan submittal to avoid any time delays. Submit a completed New Address Request Application and site plan to BusinessAssistance@anaheim.net. You will be contacted via email with a link for payment on the AnaheimNext website. If submitting in-person, please arrive by 11:00 am to ensure same day processing.
auditTable.note: No legal authority is cited for the new address request. The checklist mentions a payment link but doesn't state the fee, so the fee is unknown.

The covenant for the JADU will be drafted by the City Attorney’s office and must be recorded with the Orange County Clerk-Recorder’s office prior to the issuance of a building permit. The covenant will specify the following, at a minimum:
▪ The JADU shall not be sold or owned separately from the main dwelling and the parcel upon which the unit is located and shall not be subdivided in any manner that would authorize such sale or ownership;

(b) requires owner occupancy only for JADUs that share sanitation, but the covenant's no-separate-sale clause does match § 66333, subd. (c). Possible conflict, confirm with city staff or counsel.

## Fast Path Check: Anaheim, ADU
**Date checked:** 2026-11-07 · **Prototype · not legal advice**

### At a glance
| Path found | Stale citations | Possible conflicts | Package gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADU / JADU ministerial approval | 2 | 1 | no package provided |

### Findings
We reviewed the City of Anaheim's Accessory Dwelling Unit Submittal Requirements Checklist (Z412) (dated NOV 2025) against State ADU Law (Gov. Code, §§ 66310–66342) on 2026-11-07. Of its 8 lines, 1 may not match current state law, as noted below.

1. **Line p1-5 (page 1) – *Owner Occupancy*** – The checklist states, "☐ 1. OWNER OCCUPANCY COVENANT: AMC Section 18.38.015.110 requires the recordation of an owner occupancy covenant for all JADUs, authorized by the California Government Code Sections 65852.2 and 65852.22. The covenant for the JADU will be drafted by the City Attorney’s office and must be recorded wi…" However, Gov. Code, § 66333, subd. (b) requires owner occupancy for a JADU only when it shares sanitation facilities with the main house. It isn't required when the JADU has its own bathroom, or when the owner is a governmental agency, land trust or housing organization. Separately, SB 477 (2024) renumbered Gov. Code, §§ 65852.2 and 65852.22 as §§ 66310–66342. Current sections: 65852.2 → 66310–66342 (ADU approvals: 66314–66331); 65852.22 → 66333–66339 (owner-occupancy and deed restriction: 66333). **Suggested fix:** Replace 65852.2 and 65852.22 with Gov. Code, § 66333, and apply the owner-occupancy clause only to JADUs that share sanitation with the main house. *Possible conflict, confirm with city staff or counsel.* ([source](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=66333), checked 2026-11-07)

**What the city can do:** update the checklist to cite the current sections, and review each possible conflict with city staff or counsel. This is a prototype check, not an HCD finding.

### 1. Path and legal clock
- **Path:** ADU / JADU ministerial approval
- **Clock:** 15 business days to decide completeness, with a written list of every incomplete item and how to fix it (deemed complete if late), then 60 days from a complete application to approve or deny (deemed approved if late). Source: [Gov. Code, § 66317, subds. (a)(2)–(a)(3), hand-checked in a browser 2026-11-07, per reference/sources.md; the HCD ADU Handbook (Mar 2026), pp. 14 and 34–35, cites the same rule (Gov. Code, § 66317, subd. (a)(2)(A) and (a)(3))](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=66317), checked 2026-11-07.
- **Why this path:** The ADU / JADU ministerial approval path fits because this is an ADU project and Anaheim's Z412 checklist has Planning review zoning compliance during Building plan check, which falls under the state clock (15 business days for completeness, then 60 days to approve or deny; Gov. Code, § 66317, subds. (a)(2)–(a)(3), per the browser hand-check in reference/sources.md and the HCD ADU Handbook (Mar 2026), pp. 14 and 34–35, https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/policy-and-research/adu-handbook-update.pdf, checked 2026-11-07; leginfo was not read live). The data names no alternative path, such as SB 9 (2021) or a § 66323 unit, as evaluated, so no other path was confirmed; ASSUMPTION: the project is a standard ADU or JADU and not a § 66323-only unit.
